_note: Pre-written alert responses for every type in analytics.common.ALERT_MODULES. Audience: campus electrical technician. No test limits are stated (they must come from the standard / the transformer nameplate). Wording is advisory and unreviewed by a domain expert.

actions.ack_reply: Acknowledged. I have seen this alert and will follow the checklist.
actions.snooze_reply: Snoozed for 1 hour. The alert will not notify again for this type until then. Check it before the snooze ends if you can.
actions.escalate_template: TRANSFORMER ALERT - {title} ({severity}) at {time}. {value_line}Dataset: {dataset}{sim}. Technician has seen it and needs an engineer to review. Details: {meaning}

loading_high.title: High transformer loading
loading_high.push: Load is above the alert level. Check load and cooling.
loading_high.meaning: The load current is higher than the level set for this transformer. Sustained high load heats the windings and uses up insulation life faster than normal.
loading_high.safe_to_wait: A short peak is tolerable. If it stays high for hours, do not wait.
do_now: Read the live load at the panel and confirm it matches the app
Shed or move non-essential load if you can
Look at the cooling: radiators and fans clear, oil temperature gauge not climbing
check: Which feeders draw the most current
Whether this is a short peak or has lasted hours
loading_high.escalate_if: Load stays above the alert level for another hour, or oil temperature keeps rising after you reduce load.

overcurrent.title: Overcurrent
overcurrent.push: Current is above the allowed level. Check load and connections.
overcurrent.meaning: At least one phase is carrying more current than the alert level. This can be real overload, or a fault or imbalance elsewhere on the LV side.
overcurrent.safe_to_wait: No, if it is sustained. Find out whether it is a genuine overload.
do_now: Read the three phase currents at the panel
Reduce load where you safely can
Check the LV side for any recent switching or a feeder that has tripped
check: Whether all three phases are high or only one
Terminals and lugs for heat marks or discolouration
overcurrent.escalate_if: Current stays high after load is reduced, or you see burning smell, noise or hot terminals.

hot_spot_high.title: Winding hot-spot too high
hot_spot_high.push: Estimated winding hot-spot is high. Reduce load, check cooling.
hot_spot_high.meaning: The twin estimates the hottest point inside the winding is above the alert level. This value is calculated by the model, not measured directly, so treat it as an estimate. Heat at this point is what ages the insulation.
hot_spot_high.safe_to_wait: No. Heat damage to insulation is cumulative and cannot be undone.
do_now: Reduce the load if you can
Check radiators, fans and the oil temperature gauge on site
Confirm the top-oil temperature reading is also high; if only the estimate is high, tell the engineer
check: Radiator fins blocked or covered
Any cooling fan not running
hot_spot_high.escalate_if: Hot-spot or oil temperature keeps rising after load is reduced, or cooling is visibly faulty.

top_oil_high.title: Top-oil temperature high
top_oil_high.push: Oil temperature is above the alert level. Check cooling and load.
top_oil_high.meaning: The oil at the top of the tank is hotter than the alert level. Either the load is high, the cooling is not removing heat, or the ambient is unusually hot.
top_oil_high.safe_to_wait: Not if it keeps rising. Check the cause the same day.
do_now: Compare the app value with the temperature gauge on the tank
Reduce load if you can
Check radiators and fans
check: Ambient temperature and ventilation around the unit
Whether the load explains the rise
top_oil_high.escalate_if: Temperature keeps climbing with load reduced, or the gauge and the app disagree by a large amount.

ageing_rate_high.title: Insulation ageing faster than normal
ageing_rate_high.push: Insulation is ageing faster than normal. Review load and cooling.
ageing_rate_high.meaning: The model estimates the insulation is using up its life faster than it would at normal operating temperature. One short spell is minor; a sustained rate shortens the transformer's life.
ageing_rate_high.safe_to_wait: A brief spell can wait for the next working day. A repeating pattern should be fixed.
do_now: Note when it started and what the load was
Reduce peak load if this repeats
Plan a cooling system inspection
check: Whether it happens at the same time every day
Radiators and fans
ageing_rate_high.escalate_if: It repeats daily or the rate stays high for several days.

residual_drift.title: Oil is running hotter than the twin predicts
residual_drift.push: Measured oil temp is above the twin's prediction. Possible cooling problem.
residual_drift.meaning: The twin predicts the oil temperature from load and ambient. The real reading is persistently higher than that prediction. The usual cause is reduced cooling (blocked or fouled radiators, a failed fan, low oil), but it can also be a sensor problem.
residual_drift.safe_to_wait: It builds up slowly, so a planned inspection soon is fine. Do not leave it for weeks.
do_now: Inspect radiators for blockage, dust or damage
Check fans and any oil pumps run
Check the oil level gauge
check: Compare the gauge on the tank with the app reading
Whether the load is normal while temperature is not
residual_drift.escalate_if: The gap keeps growing, the oil level is low, or the cooling looks fine but the temperature stays high.

current_unbalance.title: Phase current unbalance
current_unbalance.push: The three phase currents are uneven. Check loads and connections.
current_unbalance.meaning: The load is not shared evenly across the three phases. Heavy unbalance causes extra heating and neutral current, and often means single-phase loads are badly distributed or a connection is loose.
current_unbalance.safe_to_wait: Usually yes for a few days, unless it is severe or a connection looks hot.
do_now: Read the three phase currents at the panel
Check LV terminals and the neutral connection
Move single-phase loads between phases where possible
check: Loose or discoloured lugs
A single feeder with an unusually large load
current_unbalance.escalate_if: Unbalance is severe, the neutral is hot, or one phase has dropped to near zero.

voltage_unbalance.title: Voltage unbalance
voltage_unbalance.push: Phase voltages are uneven. Check supply and tap setting.
voltage_unbalance.meaning: The phase voltages differ more than the alert level. The cause is often on the supply side or a loose connection, not the transformer itself.
voltage_unbalance.safe_to_wait: Usually a few days, unless equipment is being damaged.
do_now: Measure the three phase voltages at the LV terminals
Check connections on the incoming side
Note the tap position
check: Whether the unbalance is also on the supply side
Any single-phase fault or blown fuse upstream
voltage_unbalance.escalate_if: Unbalance is large or connected equipment is tripping or running badly.

voltage_high.title: Voltage high
voltage_high.push: Voltage is above the allowed level. Check supply and tap setting.
voltage_high.meaning: The voltage is above the alert level. It may come from the supply, an unsuitable tap position, or light load on the grid.
voltage_high.safe_to_wait: A few days is usually fine. High voltage over a long time stresses insulation and connected equipment.
do_now: Measure the voltage at the LV terminals
Check the tap changer position
Tell the utility if the supply is high
check: Whether it is high at all times or only at night or light load
voltage_high.escalate_if: Voltage is well above the limit or sensitive equipment is being affected.

voltage_low.title: Voltage low
voltage_low.push: Voltage is below the allowed level. Check supply and tap setting.
voltage_low.meaning: The voltage is below the alert level. Causes include a weak supply, heavy load, or a tap position that does not suit the incoming voltage.
voltage_low.safe_to_wait: A few days is usually fine, but low voltage makes motors draw more current.
do_now: Measure the voltage at the LV terminals
Check the tap changer position
Check for heavy motor loads starting up
check: Whether it dips only at peak load
voltage_low.escalate_if: Voltage stays low, or equipment trips on undervoltage.

oil_low.title: Oil level low
oil_low.push: Oil level is below the alert level. Inspect for leaks.
oil_low.meaning: The oil level reading is lower than the alert level. Oil cools and insulates the windings; too little exposes them.
oil_low.safe_to_wait: No. Check it the same day.
do_now: Read the oil level gauge on the tank
Look for oil on the ground, tank, gaskets and bushings
Do not top up oil yourself unless your procedure says so
check: Whether the gauge agrees with the app
Fresh oil stains
oil_low.escalate_if: The gauge confirms low oil or you find a leak.

oil_leak.title: Possible oil leak
oil_leak.push: Oil level is falling steadily. Inspect tank and gaskets.
oil_leak.meaning: The oil level is dropping slowly and steadily, which is how a leak looks. A slow leak can go unnoticed until the level is dangerously low.
do_now: Walk around the tank and check gaskets, valves, bushings and welds for oil
Read the oil level gauge
Check the ground beneath the unit
check: Whether the app trend and the gauge agree
Any recent maintenance that may explain a drop
oil_leak.escalate_if: You find oil, or the gauge confirms the drop.

oil_theft.title: Sudden oil level drop
oil_theft.push: Oil level dropped suddenly. Inspect the site now.
oil_theft.meaning: The oil level fell by a large step in a short time and did not recover. A fast drop like this is more consistent with oil being drained than with a slow leak. It can also be a sensor fault or maintenance work, so confirm on site before drawing conclusions.
do_now: Go to the unit and read the oil level gauge
Look for drain valve opened, cut seals, spilled oil or signs of tampering
Check whether any maintenance or sampling was done today
Do not touch the unit if it looks unsafe
check: Whether the drain valve and sampling points are intact
Whether the gauge agrees with the app
oil_theft.escalate_if: The gauge confirms a real drop or you see tampering. Inform security and your supervisor.

through_fault.title: Through-fault recorded
through_fault.push: A fault current passed through the transformer. Log it.
through_fault.meaning: A short-circuit current flowed through the transformer and was cleared by protection elsewhere. The transformer itself was not the fault location, but each event adds mechanical stress to the windings.
through_fault.safe_to_wait: Yes for one event. Record it and review at the next maintenance.
do_now: Log the date, time and size of the event
Check what tripped downstream and why
Look at the tank for any visible damage or oil leaking
check: Protection relay records
Whether the transformer is still behaving normally
through_fault.escalate_if: Several events have happened in a short time, or you see any damage, noise or oil leak.

through_fault_stress.title: Fault stress building up
through_fault_stress.push: Cumulative fault stress has crossed the alert level. Plan impedance test.
through_fault_stress.meaning: Repeated through-faults add up. The accumulated stress is now above the alert level, which means the windings may have been mechanically strained. A short-circuit impedance measurement can show whether they have moved.
through_fault_stress.safe_to_wait: Plan the test within a week. Avoid avoidable heavy loading until then.
do_now: Tell the engineer and ask for a short-circuit impedance (%X) test
List the recent fault events
Check for any unusual noise
check: The number and dates of through-fault events
Whether the cause of the faults has been fixed
through_fault_stress.escalate_if: Always raise with the engineer: this needs a test, not just a look.

jump_sensor.title: Sensor reading jumped
jump_sensor.push: A sensor value jumped in a way the transformer could not. Check the sensor.
jump_sensor.meaning: A reading changed by an amount the transformer physically cannot, so the more likely cause is the sensor or its wiring, not the transformer. This points to the device, not the asset.
jump_sensor.safe_to_wait: Yes for the transformer. Check the sensor in the next day or two.
do_now: Compare the app value with the local gauge or meter
Check the sensor cable and connector
Note which channel it is
check: Loose connector or damaged cable
Whether other channels look normal
jump_sensor.escalate_if: The local gauge disagrees with the app for the same reading, or the jumps keep repeating.

range_sensor.title: Sensor value out of range
range_sensor.push: A sensor reads outside its possible range. Check the sensor.
range_sensor.meaning: A reading is outside the range this quantity can have. The sensor, its scaling or its wiring is the likely problem. Check the device, not the transformer.
range_sensor.safe_to_wait: For the transformer yes, but the channel cannot be trusted until fixed.
do_now: Compare with the local gauge or meter
Check the sensor wiring and configuration
Mark this channel as untrusted until checked
check: Sensor calibration or scaling setting
Cable damage
range_sensor.escalate_if: The sensor cannot be fixed on site or several channels show the same.

stuck_sensor.title: Sensor stuck
stuck_sensor.push: A sensor value is not changing. It may be frozen.
stuck_sensor.meaning: A reading has stayed exactly the same for longer than it normally would while other readings move. The sensor or its data link may be frozen. Check the device, not the transformer.
stuck_sensor.safe_to_wait: For the transformer yes. Check the sensor within a day or two.
do_now: Look at the local gauge and compare with the app
Check the sensor power and data cable
Restart the logger or gateway if your procedure allows
check: Whether the gauge value is moving
Whether only one channel is frozen
stuck_sensor.escalate_if: The sensor stays frozen after a restart or the gauge also looks stuck.

dead_channel.title: No data from a channel
dead_channel.push: A sensor channel is giving no data. Check the sensor and link.
dead_channel.meaning: A channel has stopped sending valid values. This is a data problem: sensor, cable, gateway or power. While it is dead the app cannot warn about that quantity.
dead_channel.safe_to_wait: The transformer is not at risk from this alert alone, but you are blind on that channel. Fix it soon.
do_now: Check which channel is dead
Check the sensor power, cable and gateway
Read the local gauge by hand until it is fixed
check: Network or gateway connection
Whether other channels are also missing
dead_channel.escalate_if: Several channels are dead, or the main temperature or current channels are lost.

drift_sensor.title: Sensor drifting
drift_sensor.push: A sensor is drifting in a way the transformer could not cause.
drift_sensor.meaning: A reading is moving slowly in a direction that the transformer could not cause on its own, for example oil level rising without a refill. A drifting sensor is the likely cause. Check the device, not the transformer.
drift_sensor.safe_to_wait: Yes for the transformer. Plan a sensor check or recalibration within a week.
do_now: Compare with the local gauge
Note how far it has drifted
Plan recalibration or replacement
check: Sensor age and last calibration
Whether a refill or maintenance explains it
drift_sensor.escalate_if: The gauge also differs from earlier readings in an unexplained way.

implausible_sensor.title: Reading is physically implausible
implausible_sensor.push: A reading contradicts the transformer's physics. Check the sensor.
implausible_sensor.meaning: The twin's physics says this reading cannot be true given the other readings, for example a temperature rising faster than the load could cause. A sensor fault is the likely explanation. Check the device first.
implausible_sensor.safe_to_wait: Check within a day. If the gauge agrees with the app, treat it as real and escalate.
do_now: Compare with the local gauge
Check the sensor and cable
If the gauge agrees with the app, treat it as a real event
check: Which reading looks wrong
Other channels at the same time
implausible_sensor.escalate_if: The local gauge confirms the unusual value.

short_circuit_trip.title: Short-circuit trip
short_circuit_trip.push: A short-circuit current tripped the transformer. Do not re-energise yet.
short_circuit_trip.meaning: A very large fault current passed through the windings. Even if protection cleared it, the force can move or loosen the windings.
short_circuit_trip.safe_to_wait: No. Keep it off until it has been inspected.
do_now: Confirm the breaker is open and the unit is isolated
Read the protection relay record: time, current and which element operated
Look at the tank for bulging, oil leaks or a burnt smell
check: Relay and event records
Oil level and gas relay (Buchholz) indication
short_circuit_trip.escalate_if: You see damage, oil leaking or a gas relay operation.

turn_fault.title: Possible shorted turns
turn_fault.push: One winding is running hotter than the load explains.
turn_fault.meaning: The winding temperature is higher than the twin predicts while the oil temperature is normal. A shorted turn heats a small part of one winding and can grow into a full winding fault.
turn_fault.safe_to_wait: No. Plan to take it out of service soon.
do_now: Compare the three winding temperatures and phase currents
Reduce load if you can while you investigate
Arrange winding resistance and turns-ratio tests
check: Winding temperature against load
Gas relay and oil sample if available
turn_fault.escalate_if: The temperature keeps rising, or a gas relay alarms.

earth_leakage.title: Earth leakage from a winding
earth_leakage.push: Current is leaking from a winding to the tank.
earth_leakage.meaning: A current is flowing from the windings to the tank or earth. This means the insulation between a winding and the tank is breaking down, which can end in an earth fault.
earth_leakage.safe_to_wait: No. Inspect within a day; sooner if it is rising.
do_now: Check the tank earth connection and the earth current reading
Look for tracking or damage on bushings
Arrange an insulation resistance test
check: Whether the leakage is steady or rising
Moisture in the oil
earth_leakage.escalate_if: The leakage rises quickly or the protection operates.

moisture_high.title: Moisture in the oil
moisture_high.push: Moisture in the oil is above the watch level.
moisture_high.meaning: Water in the oil and paper lowers the insulation strength and speeds up ageing. It usually enters through a failed breather or a leaking gasket.
moisture_high.safe_to_wait: Not for long. Dry-out is cheaper than a failure.
do_now: Check the breather and the silica gel colour
Inspect gaskets and the conservator for a leak
Take an oil sample for moisture and breakdown voltage
check: Moisture trend over the last days
Oil temperature, since warm oil holds more water
moisture_high.escalate_if: Breakdown voltage falls or moisture keeps rising after the breather is fixed.

silica_gel_exhausted.title: Silica gel used up
silica_gel_exhausted.push: The breather silica gel needs replacing.
silica_gel_exhausted.meaning: The breather dries the air that enters the conservator. When the gel has changed colour it no longer protects the oil from moisture.
silica_gel_exhausted.safe_to_wait: A few days is fine, but fix it before the next damp spell.
do_now: Look at the gel colour in the breather
Replace or recharge the gel
Check the oil seal cup at the bottom of the breather
check: Whether the oil moisture reading has started to rise
silica_gel_exhausted.escalate_if: The gel turns colour again within days, which points to a leak in the breather.

charging_current.title: Idle line being charged
charging_current.push: The transformer is charging an idle cable or line.
charging_current.meaning: With almost no load, the capacitance of an energised cable or line draws a leading current through the transformer. It is harmless in small amounts but wastes capacity and can raise voltage.
charging_current.safe_to_wait: Yes. This is not damaging by itself.
do_now: Find out which feeder or cable is energised with no load
Switch it out if it is not needed
check: Whether the supply voltage rises when load is low
charging_current.escalate_if: The voltage keeps climbing at light load.

efficiency_low.title: Efficiency below expected
efficiency_low.push: The transformer is losing more energy than it should.
efficiency_low.meaning: The measured efficiency is below what the nameplate losses predict for this load. Extra losses become heat and cost money.
efficiency_low.safe_to_wait: For a few days, while you look into it.
do_now: Compare the load, power factor and harmonics
Look for hot joints with a thermal camera
Check the cooling and the oil temperature
check: Whether winding temperature is higher than the load explains
efficiency_low.escalate_if: Efficiency keeps falling or temperature rises.

temp_rise_fast.title: Oil temperature rising fast
temp_rise_fast.meaning: The oil is heating faster than weather or load usually explain. A cooling fault, a blocked radiator or a sudden overload can do this.
do_now: Read the oil and winding temperature gauges
Check the load and reduce it if you can
Check the fans, pumps and radiator valves
check: Whether the load changed at the same time
temp_rise_fast.escalate_if: The temperature reaches the alarm setting.

frequency_off.title: Supply frequency off
frequency_off.push: The supply frequency is outside the normal band.
frequency_off.meaning: Frequency should stay close to the grid value. A large deviation points to a grid or generator problem, not the transformer.
do_now: Check the grid or generator source
Ask the utility whether there is a disturbance
check: Whether other equipment shows the same
frequency_off.escalate_if: It stays out of band for long.
